**Aspose.PDF FOSS for C++ 1.0.1** is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed C++20 library for working
with PDF documents. It can open, render, edit, and create PDFs, and it links against nothing but
the C++ standard library. Every codec and the page rasteriser are implemented from scratch. The
public API is a strict subset of Aspose.PDF for .NET, so class and method names will be familiar
to anyone migrating from .NET.

## What's new in 1.0.1

- **NuGet package for Visual Studio.** [`Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS)
  ships static libraries for x64, x86, and ARM64, in Release (`/MD`) and Debug (`/MDd`). It adds
  the include path, links the matching library, and raises the project to C++20. Install it and
  write `#include <aspose.pdf.foss.hpp>`.
- **Self-contained Debug libraries.** The Debug library in the Windows zip, and the Debug libraries
  in the NuGet package, now embed their debug information (`/Z7`). Linking them no longer produces
  LNK4099 "PDB not found" warnings.

The library code and public API are unchanged from 1.0.0.

## Highlights

- **Open, edit, and save PDFs.** Byte-verbatim round-trips, incremental `/Info` metadata updates,
  and password-protected files (`Document(path, password)`).
- **Extract text.** `TextAbsorber` covers a whole document or one page; `TextFragmentAbsorber`
  gives positioned fragments with font, size, and colour.
- **Render pages** to PNG, JPEG, BMP, and TIFF with a built-in anti-aliased rasteriser. That
  includes multi-page TIFF and 1/4/8-bpp palettised output.
- **Create documents from scratch** with positioned and wrapped text, tables, vector graphics
  (`Line`, `Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`), images, and watermarks.
- **Annotations** across 13 subtypes, each with a pre-generated appearance stream, plus
  **AcroForm fields** (text box, checkbox, radio button, combo box, list box, button) with
  `Form::Flatten()`.
- **Security:** RC4-40/128 and AES-128/256 encryption and decryption, and detached PKCS#7 digital
  signatures.
- **Navigation:** outlines (bookmarks), named destinations, page labels, and embedded files.
- **Classic Facades API:** `PdfConverter`, `PdfExtractor`, `PdfFileEditor`, `PdfFileSecurity`,
  `PdfFileSignature`, `PdfFileStamp`, `PdfBookmarkEditor`, `FormEditor`, and more.

The full list of changes is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Cpp/blob/v1.0.1/CHANGELOG.md).

## Downloads

| Asset | Platform | Toolchain | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aspose-pdf-foss-cpp-1.0.1-linux-x64-gcc13.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64 | GCC 13, libstdc++, built on Ubuntu 24.04 | `libaspose_pdf_foss.a` (Release, position-independent) |
| `aspose-pdf-foss-cpp-1.0.1-windows-x64-msvc.zip` | Windows x64 | MSVC (Visual Studio 2022), dynamic CRT | `aspose_pdf_foss.lib` (Release, `/MD`) and `aspose_pdf_fossd.lib` (Debug, `/MDd`) |
| `Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS.1.0.1.nupkg` | Windows x64, x86, ARM64 | Visual Studio 2022+ (MSBuild) | The NuGet package, also published on [nuget.org](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS) |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | — | — | SHA-256 checksums of the archives |
| Source code (zip / tar.gz) | any | any C++20 compiler | Full source tree, generated by GitHub |

Every archive contains:

- `include/`: the public headers, including the single-entry header `aspose.pdf.foss.hpp`.
- `lib/`: the static library and the CMake package files (`lib/cmake/aspose_pdf_foss/`).
- `share/doc/aspose_pdf_foss/`: `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, and the OFL 1.1 text for the
  bundled fonts.
- `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `BUILDINFO.txt` (exact compiler and commit used for the
  build).

Each archive was built, tested, and then compiled and run as a `find_package` consumer before it
was attached to this release. To verify a download:
`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`.

## Getting started

### Visual Studio (NuGet)

Install [`Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS) through
**Manage NuGet Packages**, or from the Package Manager Console:

```powershell
Install-Package Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS
```

The package adds the include path, links the library that matches your platform (x64, Win32, or
ARM64) and configuration, and raises the project to C++20. Your code only needs
`#include <aspose.pdf.foss.hpp>`.

### From a release archive (CMake)

Extract the archive, then point CMake at it:

```cmake
find_package(aspose_pdf_foss 1.0 CONFIG REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(your_app PRIVATE aspose_pdf_foss::aspose_pdf_foss)
```

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/aspose-pdf-foss-cpp-1.0.1-linux-x64-gcc13
```

The imported target switches your target to C++20 automatically. On Windows, CMake selects the
Release or Debug library to match your configuration.

### From source (CMake subdirectory)

```cmake
add_subdirectory(Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Cpp)
target_link_libraries(your_app PRIVATE aspose_pdf_foss::aspose_pdf_foss)
```

Building from source needs CMake 3.20+, a C++20 compiler (GCC 13+, Clang 16+, or MSVC 2022 17.5+),
and Python 3 at build time only.

### Hello, PDF

```cpp
#include <aspose.pdf.foss.hpp>
#include <fstream>
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    Aspose::Pdf::Document doc("input.pdf");
    std::cout << "Pages: " << doc.Pages().Count() << "\n";

    Aspose::Pdf::Text::TextAbsorber absorber;
    absorber.Visit(doc);
    std::cout << absorber.Text() << "\n";

    Aspose::Pdf::Devices::PngDevice png(Aspose::Pdf::Devices::Resolution(150));
    std::ofstream out("page1.png", std::ios::binary);
    png.Process(doc.Pages()[1], out);
}
```

The [`examples/`](https://github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Cpp/tree/v1.0.1/examples)
directory has 12 more runnable programs, including a 10-page from-scratch showcase.

## Compatibility

- **Language:** C++20. The public headers use C++20 standard-library features such as `std::span`.
- **Prebuilt Linux library:** link with GCC 13 or newer, or with Clang against libstdc++ 13 or
  newer, on a system with glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04 or later). For other distributions or
  toolchains, build from source.
- **Prebuilt Windows libraries (zip and NuGet):** link with the same or a newer MSVC toolset,
  using the dynamic CRT (`/MD` for Release, `/MDd` for Debug). This is the CMake and Visual Studio
  default. Debug libraries carry embedded debug info, so no separate PDB is needed.
- **Runtime dependencies:** none.

## Known limitations

- The `XmpValue` helpers `IsDateTime`, `IsField`, `IsNamedValue`, `IsRaw`, `IsNamedValues`, and
  `IsStructure` are stubs that always return `false`. Use `IsString`, `IsInteger`, `IsDouble`, and
  `IsArray` instead.
- Standard-14 fallback fonts cover Helvetica, Times-Roman, and Courier (four styles each). Symbol
  and ZapfDingbats have no bundled fallback.
- Setting metadata on a from-scratch document and then saving throws, because the incremental
  writer can only patch an existing `/Info` object.
- Objects added to `Paragraphs`, `Annotations`, `Form`, `Artifacts`, and `Outlines` are stored by
  reference, so they must outlive `Save()`.
- Encryption permissions are enforced by PDF viewers; the library is not a DRM mechanism.

[Aspose.PDF for C++ Enterprise Edition](https://products.aspose.com/pdf/cpp/) does not have these
limitations and covers a broader feature set.
